title: SDK context fanout with rate-limited trace hooks and bounded header propagation
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: High-QPS SDKs in edge services are producing large context headers and unbounded per-request trace fanout to worker pools. This causes increased tail latency in proxies and inflates downstream ingress costs (network and ingestion). We also see noisy traces where sampled spans blow up memory on collector side during bursts.

Goal: Implement an SDK-side instrumentation hook that: 1) rate-limits and coalesces outbound trace header updates for high-frequency callers; 2) enforces a bounded propagation header size (with deterministic truncation and a small rehydration hint); 3) provides a configurable fanout strategy for local worker queues that avoids creating full child spans per work unit by default (use lightweight continuation tokens + optional child span creation if selected via rollout); and 4) exposes metrics and logs to validate correctness and performance (propagation_size_bytes histogram, sampled_span_drop_count, fanout_rewrite_count).

Why unique: Existing propagation changes focus on header normalization and compatibility. This ticket is focused on operational cost and tail-latency reduction for high-throughput SDK users by combining sampling-aware rate limiting, header bounding, and a new continuation token pattern that reduces span cardinality while preserving traceability for debugging when needed.

Non-goals: This is not a replacement for cross-service trace format compatibility work (we still keep W3C traceparent) nor does it change collector-side sampling policies (those are separate).
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes (a) a transparent hook enabled by default that coalesces header writes for identical context within a 10ms bucket; (b) a max-propagation-bytes default of 1024 with deterministic truncation and trace-hint header for rehydration; (c) a fanout continuation token format documented and backward compatible; (d) control flags for customers to opt into child-span fanout per route.
End-to-end latency p95 for the edge proxy with the SDK enabled improves by >= 7% on our internal high-QPS benchmark compared to current baseline (same CPU/memory).
propagation_size_bytes histogram emitted to observability metrics and surfaced in console route analytics for at least 3 test routes.
Automated unit and integration tests covering header truncation, continuation token parsing, and sampled/un-sampled behavior exist and run in CI.
Graceful fallback: when the SDK detects an older downstream agent that cannot handle continuation tokens, it falls back to existing traceparent-only propagation without causing errors.

implementation_notes: Coalescing: group outgoing propagation header writes by (trace_id, sampled_flag, keyset_hash) within 10ms window; first write wins for deterministic ordering.

Bounded headers: prefer to keep traceparent + baggage keys; deterministic truncation removes lower-priority baggage entries and emits X-RW-Trace-Hint header with hash+offset for collector rehydration when available.
Continuation token: compact binary blob base64-encoded containing parent_span_id, sampling_flag, and minimal KV pointers. Backwards compatible via presence/absence of X-RW-Cont header.

Fanout: worker queues accept continuation token and create lightweight local child spans only when route flag 'allow_child_fanout' is enabled; otherwise workers link logs to parent via local metadata.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Truncation may remove debugging baggage needed for incident triage. Mitigation: default keep-list of critical keys (request-id,user-id,route) and Console surfaced 'missing-baggage' alert during canary.
Risk: New header formats may be dropped by intermediaries. Mitigation: keep additions in prefixed headers (X-RW-*) and fall back to W3C traceparent only when downstream indicates incompatibility.
Risk: Metric cardinality increase from propagation_size histogram. Mitigation: bucketization and low-resolution histograms by route only, sample some routes for full resolution.
test_plan: Unit tests for truncation algorithm with synthetic baggage sets (edge-cases for unicode).
Integration test: 10k RPS synthetic harness route verifying header sizes and p95 latency delta under coalescing on/off.
Canary: Enable on internal staging routes for 48h; monitor propagation_size_bytes and sampled_span_drop_count and rollback on >10% error delta or any increase in 99th latency.
Collector compatibility test against older agent versions to ensure graceful fallback.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature behind SDK flag and environment variable by default disabled for external users (internal staging enabled).
Phase 1: Enable for 10% of production route traffic via Console rollout targeting low-risk tenants for 24h, monitor key metrics.
Phase 2: Expand to 50% after 72h if metrics stable; enable child fanout off-by-default until route owners opt-in.
Phase 3: Full rollout and deprecation window for older agent versions (announce 30d notice).
